title: Light that doesn’t move
hook: A sunbeam can be trapped in a jar.
script: A sunbeam can be trapped in a jar. What if the fastest thing in the universe could be made to crawl? By chilling atoms to near absolute zero, physicists slowed a light beam to about the pace of a rush-hour cyclist. They used Electromagnetically Induced Transparency to open a window in potassium-40 gas. Suddenly, light stumbled into a medium where it no longer obeyed its own rules. The beam crept forward at 4.57 metres a second, slower than a brisk walk. But here’s the even wilder part: they’ve frozen a pulse of light in place, stored it, and released it again moments later.
